sentences.text: Lehmanosteus is an extinct genus containing only one species of arthrodire placoderm fish.
The genus name honors the French paleontologist Jean-Pierre Lehman.
The type species Lehmanosteus hyperboreus was formally described in 1984.
Fossils were discovered in the Early Devonian Wood Bay Formation on Spitsbergen, part of the Svalbard archipelago in Norway.
Only a single fossil occurrence of Lehmanosteus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
Lehmanosteus represents one of the most basal members of the order Arthrodira.
The genus belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Lehmanosteus is classified within the class Placodermi.
The animal lived during the Pragian to Emsian stages, between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago.
